s: Seine Gefühle ihr gegenüber sind ambivalent, sowohl positiv als auch negativ.
His feelings to her are ambivalent, positive as well as negative.
ambivalent.et: From ambi-, ambo and valens (inflected valent-), valeo.

Ambition.et: Borrowed from French ambition, from Latin ambitiō.

s: ambrosia (food of gods or delicious foods)

Amboss.et: From Middle High German anebōȥ, from Old High German anabōȥ (“anvil”) (see also anabolz (“anvil”), anabelzi (“anvil”), which are cognate to Plautdietsch Aumbolt (“anvil”)). Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *bautaną.

Ambivalenz.et: Coined by Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler in 1910, from Latin ambō (“both”) and valentia (“strength”), from the verb valeō (“to be strong”).

s: Amberg (an independent town and administrative seat of Amberg-Sulzbach district, Upper Palatinate region, Bavaria, Germany)

Ambiente.et: From Italian ambiente, from Latin ambiēns, present active participle of ambiō (“to surround”). Doublet of ambient.

am Boden zerstört sein.et: Literally, “to be destroyed on the ground”.

Amblyopie.et: Borrowed from New Latin amblyōpia, from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓μβλῠωπῐ́ᾱ (ămblŭōpĭ́ā).

Ambo.et: Borrowed from Ecclesiastical Latin ambō, from Medieval Greek ἄμβων (ámbōn).
